Write-Ahead Logging

The default method by which SQLite implements atomic commit is a rollback journal. Since version 3.7.0 a write-ahead log is available as an alternative, and it changes the concurrency story substantially for readers.

Advantages¶

  1. WAL is significantly faster in most scenarios, because a commit appends rather than rewrites.
  2. WAL provides more concurrency: readers do not block writers and a writer does not block readers.
  3. Disk I/O operations tend to be more sequential, which matters a great deal on spinning media.

Activating

Set the journal mode once. It is persistent, so it survives closing and reopening the database, which is the usual source of confusion. See the note below.

PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;
SELECT * FROM t1;

Comparison

ModeReaders block writersDurable
rollbackyesyes
WALnoconfigurable

See the synchronous pragma for the durability tradeoff, which is the one thing people get wrong when they switch.
